entries.title: I Samuel 11:1
segments:
Jabesh-gilead; a city in the tribe of Manesseh, on the east side of Jordan. 
 
If it is wise in men to make great sacrifices and submit to many hardships to save their lives, how much more wise is it to sacrifice and suffer whatever may be needful to save their souls.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:2
segments: Great cruelty and bitter oposition to the people and cause of God generally go together.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:4
segments:
Gibeah; in Benjamin, where Saul lived. 
 
It is right that one portion of the human family should deeply sympathize with the sufferings of another, and do whatever may be consistent with truth and duty to afford them relief.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:6
segments: The Spirit of God; awakened Saul's indignation and inspired him with wisdom, courage, and all needful qualities to collect an army and lead them forth to victory.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:7
segments: The fear of the Lord; that he would in his providence bring dreadful judgments upon them, if they should not go forth to protect their brethren.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:8
segments: Bezek; a place between Sechem and Jabesh-gilead.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:9
segments: If gladness and joy are occasioned by deliverance from temporal calamities, much more should they be by deliverance from those which are eternal.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:11
segments: The morning-watch; between two o'clock and sunrise.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:13
segments: True courage and real greatness are manifested in forgiving personal injuries, not in avenging them.

entries.title: I Samuel 11:14
segments: Renew the kingdom; publicly proclaim Saul as king.
